ai.description: This gecko reaches 75–125 mm. It is pale grey or pinkish-brown with dark mottling. Key features include vertical pupils, toe pads, and a row of small, pointed tubercles along the tail edges.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Hemidactylus frenatus* by the presence of a distinct, sharp-edged fold of skin with small tubercles along the sides of its belly, which other common species lack.
ai.habitat: The common house gecko thrives in tropical to subtropical lowlands, typically inhabiting human dwellings, gardens, and dry deciduous forests below 1,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Common House Gecko is primarily nocturnal, often congregating near artificial lights to ambush insects attracted to the glow.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus frenatus* is oviparous, laying clutches of two hard-shelled, spherical eggs. Breeding occurs year-round in India, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus frenatus* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, occurring from sea level up to 2,000 meters in diverse habitats across most Indian states.
